subject: Biotechnology
title: Companion Diagnostics
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Companion Diagnostics.

hook.text: A companion diagnostic is a test paired with a drug — you cannot get the drug without passing the test.

buildup.text: HercepTest detects HER2 overexpression — only HER2-positive patients receive trastuzumab, the targeted antibody.

discovery.text: Cobas EGFR mutation test identifies patients who benefit from osimertinib — the drug and test are co-approved.

twist.text: Tissue-agnostic approvals break organ boundaries — larotrectinib treats any cancer with an NTRK fusion, from lung to thyroid.

climax.text: Over 50 companion diagnostics are FDA-approved — matching the right patient to the right drug at the right time.

punchline.text: Test first, treat second — companion diagnostics ensure drugs reach the right patients.

quiz.question: What is a tissue-agnostic cancer drug approval?
options: A drug approved for use in all cancer patients regardless of test results
A drug approved based on a specific genetic marker regardless of where the cancer originated
A drug that treats the tissue surrounding the tumor rather than the tumor itself

details.summary: Companion diagnostics are tests required before prescribing specific drugs, identifying patients whose tumors have the molecular target the drug addresses. They ensure drugs are given only to patients likely to benefit, improving response rates and avoiding futile treatment with expensive therapies.
details.whyItMatters: Without companion diagnostics, targeted cancer drugs would be given to all patients even though only the molecular subset benefits. These tests are essential for rational precision oncology, improving outcomes while reducing healthcare waste.
takeaways: Companion diagnostics identify patients with specific drug-targetable mutations
FDA approval of many targeted drugs requires an approved companion diagnostic
They transform cancer treatment from empirical to molecularly guided selection

faq.question: What is an example of how companion diagnostics guide cancer treatment?
faq.answer: HER2 testing is required before prescribing trastuzumab for breast cancer because only HER2-positive tumors, about 20 percent of breast cancers, respond. Without testing, 80 percent of patients would receive an expensive drug with side effects but zero benefit.

faq.question: Are companion diagnostics cost effective even though they add expense?
faq.answer: Yes. The cost of a diagnostic test is far less than futile treatment with drugs costing thousands per month. By filtering patients, companion diagnostics improve response rates from 10 to 20 percent untested to 50 to 80 percent in the selected population, dramatically improving cost effectiveness.
